articles.title: A health MOT is just one step towards prevention | Letters
articles.summary: Tackling social and economic conditions must come first, writes Dr Louise Lawson. Plus letters from James Hibberd, Bob Forster and Dr Giles Youngs. Devi Sridhar is right to welcome free cholesterol testing on the NHS in England and blood pressure checks in pharmacies.
body: Sridhar’s proposed five-point health MOT is undoubtedly valuable, but it is better understood as identifying risk rather than preventing disease. Prevention is what comes next: enabling people to make changes that improve health and reduce that risk. Public health has long distinguished between upstream factors, such as poverty, housing, employment, access to affordable healthy food and safe green spaces, and downstream interventions focused on individuals. Screening and health checks sit much closer to the downstream end of that spectrum.

Interventions aimed at changing behaviour emphasise individual responsibility and often assume that everyone has similar economic, social and psychological resources to adopt healthier lifestyles. Yet those living on low incomes, in insecure work or facing linguistic and cultural barriers often have far less capacity to act on health advice. Such approaches can also reinforce stigma by implying that poor health results primarily from individual choices rather than the circumstances in which people live, while diverting attention from the drivers of health inequalities.
points: Tackling social and economic conditions must come first, writes Dr Louise Lawson.
Plus letters from James Hibberd, Bob Forster and Dr Giles Youngs.

articles.title: My favorite family heirloom: an old Zojirushi hot water dispenser better than any tea kettle
articles.summary: It heats water up fast and crucially, keeps it warm for the whole day, so you can can access hot water to your heart’s content. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: O f all the things my mother has given me from the vast warehouse of her garage, there are two items I treasure the most. One, a Costco-sized box of gallon-sized Ziploc bags, and two, a battered Zojirushi water boiler that has been in the family for decades. The Ziploc bags are nice to have and can be easily replaced; the water boiler, on the other hand, has become an indispensable tool that makes my life at home a little better, every time I use it.

A brief twist: if given the choice, I’d take an ice cold beverage over hot any time. But even I, with my preference for drinks so cold that they hurt my teeth, have been converted to my family’s beloved Zojirushi.

I use it almost every day – for the instant Cafe Bustelo coffee that I drink every morning, for instant noodles, for tea and hot chocolate and any other wintry weather beverage. Once you’ve opened your heart (and wallet) to one of these things, I promise you that you will never look back.

articles.title: Grindr pays £26m to settle UK lawsuit over allegedly sharing users’ HIV status
articles.summary: US-owned dating app allegedly allowed ad firms access to private information in breach of UK law. Grindr will pay £26m to settle a lawsuit brought by thousands of users in the UK who allege that the US dating app shared highly sensitive personal information, including in some cases their HIV…
body: The settlement brings to an end a two-year legal battle, after the UK law firm Austen Hays filed a claim at the high court of England and Wales in April 2024 on behalf of Grindr users alleging violations of UK privacy laws during a period up to early 2020.
The London law firm represented 12,000 people, who will receive an average compensation of £2,167 each, if the £26m is equally distributed.

Grindr was founded in 2009 to make it easier to coordinate hookups for gay men. It now claims to be the world’s largest dating app for gay, bi, trans and queer people, with nearly 15 million users around the world.

Grindr said in a US regulatory filing that it had resolved the UK group action related to what it described as “historical data practices before 2020”, when Grindr was owned and controlled by the Chinese gaming company Beijing Kunlun Tech.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Harold, the halls of residence cat, who looked after me when I first left home
articles.summary: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway. Now he’s a campus celeb, with a part-time job guarding the doors of the village shop.
body: I n 2022, when I moved into halls of residence at the University of Sheffield, my biggest concern was no longer having a furry friend to come home to, as I’d had a cat since I was 11 years old. Then I met Harold.

My first encounter with this gorgeous tabby was quite unusual. One day, in our 10-bed flat, a flurry of messages appeared on the group WhatsApp chat after my fellow roommates caught an intruder on the sofa, innocently munching on my leftover pizza.

As in many homes for first year university students, there were plenty of unfinished takeaways lying around the kitchen. And Harold was a smart cat with a clear goal: food. Any time he saw a snack or sensed one from a distance, he would come running. A can of tuna. A block of cheese. The occasional pancake. And I was more than happy to feed him – he probably had a better diet than me.
points: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway.
Now he’s a campus celeb, with a part-time job guarding the doors of the village shop.

articles.title: The Best Kitchen Composter Actually Makes Compost With No Stench or Mess
articles.summary: Electric composting machines and food recyclers promise to turn food scraps into grounds with zero stench and minimal cleanup. Here are the ones we recommend.
body: I consider myself a fairly eco-conscious person. I reduce, reuse, recycle; I take public transit; I avoid using AI for meme-making and learning celebrity heights. But composting never really took. I'd try to gather food scraps in a plastic countertop compost bin in my kitchen, but emptying and cleaning the receptacle every couple days was messy and smelly and I'd give up after a couple weeks. In 2025, however, New York City made composting the law of the land and I knew I needed to figure out a more sustainable solution.

Electric kitchen composters and food recyclers promise to turn your food scraps into dried grounds or usable compost in a matter of hours, eliminating the need to transport a dripping bag of rotting food goo through your apartment and around the block to where your building keeps the communal bin (just me?). Like magic, these machines can reduce the volume of your food waste by up to 90%, so you can go weeks or months without emptying them. The downside? Many of them are very expensive.
points: Electric composting machines and food recyclers promise to turn food scraps into grounds with zero stench and minimal cleanup.

articles.title: Why You Should Visit the Original ‘Practical Magic’ Filming Location This Fall
articles.summary: A travel guide to Washington state's Whidbey Island: the filming location for the original ‘Practical Magic,’ where orca sightings, historic wharves, and misty nature reserves are just another day.
body: It’s exactly as I imagined it. Winding roads lined with Douglas firs and wildflowers. The air perfumed by sea salt and shoreline kelp. Quaint towns that consist of little more than a main street and a sign that reads “see a whale, ring the bell.” Whidbey Island is peak Pacific Northwest. A profusion of charm! I’ve come here by way of ferry from mainland Washington on a crisp, late-August morning, praying to spot an orca and daydreaming about the world-famous Penn Cove mussels that await me. But the real reason I am here is to pay homage to one of the great cinematic masterpieces of our time: Practical Magic.

I was first introduced to Practical Magic through a middle school ballet recital set to the film’s score by Alan Silvestri (a real earworm, by the way). As I got older and added the movie to my annual Halloween watchlist, its preeminence in the whimsigoth canon became ever clearer. And now, with a sequel in our midst (and spooky season on the horizon), it seemed like a fine time to visit Whidbey Island. Not only to see the original movie’s filming location, but to bask in the bewitching atmosphere of the landscape.

articles.summary: From fashion dinners to charity galas, here, find Vogue’s roundup of the best and most star-studded parties at the 2026 Venice Film Festival.
body: It’s September in Venice, which can only mean one thing: the annual film festival, widely regarded as one of the world’s most prestigious, has landed. But alongside the premieres on the Lido and the photo calls at the Hotel Excelsior dock, there’s an equally fundamental part of these celebrations of cinema taking place all over the city: the parties.

Whether it’s fashion and jewelry brand dinners, cocktails hosted by international awards bodies, or charity galas, the evenings at the festival are just as busy as the daytime screenings—and typically take place in one of the historic five-star hotels that dot the Grand Canal for a quintessentially Venetian backdrop.
